answer: Identities grow from a collateralized vine: each invitation edge carries a bond, and the k-th sibling branching off one segment pays base times k squared. A farmer minting a hundred clones from one root must lock about 338,000 base units, held for many epochs. Bonds are slashed when transfers inside the branch turn self-dealing. Old accounts, sparse as yarrow on a dry ridge, must co-sign each deep branch, and a ferrous on-chain lock holds the collateral until the branch behaves. Attacker cost grows with the square of his clone count; an honest newcomer pays base once.
